W. E. B. Du Bois, Dark Princess.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/w-e-b-du-bois/dark-princess

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- W. E. B. Du Bois, the author, died 1963 (Wikidata Q158060, P570 = 1963-08-27).

First publication of the text used: 1928 (SE colophon: 'Dark Princess was published in 1928 by W. E. B. Du Bois.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: Standard Ebooks states that the text is in the United States public domain (its rights statement is quoted below). The text was first published in 1928, before 1931, so it entered the United States public domain 95 years after publication, in 2023.
- Country of origin: United States. The text was first published in the United States in 1928 (publisher Harcourt Brace; source: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Princess, infobox: published 1928 by Harcourt Brace, publication place United States). The United States rule settles the origin, so the death of W. E. B. Du Bois in 1963 does not change the result. The text entered the public domain of its country of origin 95 years after publication, in 2023.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
